title: Multiplying and dividing integers; absolute value
summary: Multiply and divide negative numbers with hops on the number line, find the pattern behind the signs, and measure distance from zero.
guide: Adding a negative number is a hop to the left: {{alg:-3 + (-4)}} starts at {{num:-3}} and hops 4 to the left.
Multiplying is repeated hops from zero: {{alg:3 × (-2)}} is three hops of {{num:-2}}, so it lands on {{num:-6}}.
When a pattern goes down by one each time, the answers change by the same amount each time. Following the pattern past zero shows why a {{term:negative-number}} times a negative number is positive.
Division undoes multiplication: {{alg:(-12) ÷ 3}} asks "3 times what makes {{num:-12}}?". The answer is {{num:-4}}, because {{alg:3 × (-4) = -12}}.
The {{term:absolute-value}} of a number is its distance from zero, so it is never negative: {{alg:|-7| = 7}} and {{alg:|7| = 7}}.

engine.label-line: Number line: tap to place a point

add-a-negative.title: Adding a negative
add-a-negative.prompt: At night it was {{num:-3}} °C, and by dawn the temperature had changed by {{num:-4}} degrees. Start at {{num:-3}} (the grey dot) and tap where you land. First predict: will you end up left or right of {{num:-3}}? What is {{alg:-3 + (-4)}}?
add-a-negative.hint: Adding {{num:-4}} is a hop of 4 to the left. From {{num:-3}}, count 4 steps left.
add-a-negative.success: Well done! {{alg:-3 + (-4) = -7}}. Adding a negative number moves you left, so dawn was colder.
add-a-negative.why: Sara says "two minuses make a plus", so {{alg:-3 + (-4) = 7}}. What is wrong with her reasoning?
add-a-negative.model: The rule about two minuses is for multiplying, not adding. Adding {{num:-4}} is a hop of 4 to the left, so from {{num:-3}} we go further below zero and land on {{num:-7}}. A temperature that drops by 4 cannot suddenly become warm.

feedback.count: Put one point where the hop lands.
feedback.two-minuses: "Two minuses make a plus" is a rule for multiplying. Here you are adding {{num:-4}}: hop 4 to the left of {{num:-3}}.
feedback.hopped-right: You hopped right. That would be {{alg:-3 + 4}}. Adding {{num:-4}} means hopping to the left.
feedback.too-big: Not far enough left. Start at {{num:-3}} and hop exactly 4 to the left; the arc should say −4.
feedback.too-small: Too far left. Hop just 4 steps from {{num:-3}}; the arc should say −4.

three-hops.title: Three hops of −2
three-hops.prompt: A lift starts at the ground floor (0) and goes down 2 floors, three times. Make three hops of {{num:-2}} from zero: tap where each hop lands. Then predict: what is {{alg:3 × (-2)}}?
three-hops.hint: Each hop goes 2 to the left. Tap {{num:-2}}, then the next landing, then the next.
three-hops.success: Right! Three hops of {{num:-2}} land on {{num:-6}}, so {{alg:3 × (-2) = -6}}. The lift is on floor {{num:-6}}.
three-hops.model: Multiplying by 3 means taking a number three times. Taking {{num:-2}} three times is {{alg:(-2) + (-2) + (-2)}}: three hops of 2 to the left, which land on {{num:-6}}.

feedback.count: Put three points: one where each hop of {{num:-2}} lands.
feedback.hopped-right: Your hops go to the right. That is {{alg:3 × 2}}. A hop of {{num:-2}} goes 2 to the left.
feedback.wrong: Every hop must be exactly 2 to the left of the last one: {{num:-2}}, then {{num:-4}}, then … .

sign-pattern.title: Follow the pattern
sign-pattern.prompt: The dark dots show {{alg:3 × (-2) = -6}}, {{alg:2 × (-2) = -4}}, {{alg:1 × (-2) = -2}} and {{alg:0 × (-2) = 0}}. Each time the first number goes down by 1, the answer goes up by 2. Carry the pattern on: place {{alg:(-1) × (-2)}}, then {{alg:(-2) × (-2)}}, then {{alg:(-3) × (-2)}}.
sign-pattern.hint: From {{num:-6}} to {{num:-4}} to {{num:-2}} to 0, each answer is 2 more. So the next one is 2 more than 0.
sign-pattern.success: Excellent! The pattern carries on past zero: 2, 4, 6. So {{alg:(-3) × (-2) = 6}}.
sign-pattern.why: Use the pattern to explain why a negative number times a negative number is positive.
sign-pattern.model: In the list {{alg:3 × (-2)}}, {{alg:2 × (-2)}}, {{alg:1 × (-2)}}, {{alg:0 × (-2)}} the answers go up by 2 each time: {{num:-6}}, {{num:-4}}, {{num:-2}}, 0. The pattern doesn't stop at zero, so the next answers are 2, 4, 6. That means {{alg:(-1) × (-2) = 2}} and {{alg:(-3) × (-2) = 6}}.

feedback.count: Put three points: the answers to {{alg:(-1) × (-2)}}, {{alg:(-2) × (-2)}} and {{alg:(-3) × (-2)}}.
feedback.minus-stays: Look at the dark dots: the answers are climbing towards zero, 2 more each time. The pattern doesn't turn back at zero; it keeps climbing.
feedback.wrong: Keep adding 2: after 0 come 2, then 4, then 6.

share-the-drop.title: Share the drop
share-the-drop.prompt: Over 3 hours the temperature fell by 12 degrees, the same amount each hour. That is {{alg:(-12) ÷ 3}}. The dark dot is {{num:-12}}. Tap where one hour's change lands, starting from 0.
share-the-drop.hint: Three equal hops from 0 must reach {{num:-12}}. How big is one hop? Ask: 3 times what is {{num:-12}}?
share-the-drop.success: Right! {{alg:(-12) ÷ 3 = -4}}, because {{alg:3 × (-4) = -12}}. The temperature fell 4 degrees each hour.
share-the-drop.why: How can you check {{alg:(-12) ÷ 3 = -4}} with multiplication? And is {{alg:12 ÷ 3}} the same as {{alg:3 ÷ 12}}?
share-the-drop.model: Division undoes multiplication: {{alg:3 × (-4) = -12}}, so {{alg:(-12) ÷ 3 = -4}}. Swapping the numbers changes a division: {{alg:12 ÷ 3 = 4}}, but {{alg:3 ÷ 12}} is only a quarter.

feedback.count: Put one point: the change in one hour.
feedback.sign-lost: The temperature is falling, so each hour's change is negative. Check: {{alg:3 × 4 = 12}}, not {{num:-12}}.
feedback.added: That is {{alg:-12 + 3}}. We need to share {{num:-12}} into 3 equal steps.
feedback.too-big: Not far enough. Three hops of this size wouldn't reach {{num:-12}}.
feedback.too-small: Too far. Three hops of this size would go past {{num:-12}}.

distance-from-zero.title: Five floors away
distance-from-zero.prompt: Ali's lift is 5 floors away from the ground floor (0), but he doesn't say whether it is up or down. Place every floor it could be on. Then use the {{term:absolute-value}}: which numbers have {{alg:|x| = 5}}?
distance-from-zero.hint: Being 5 away from zero can mean 5 steps to the right or 5 steps to the left.
distance-from-zero.success: Well done! 5 and {{num:-5}} are both 5 away from zero, so {{alg:|5| = 5}} and {{alg:|-5| = 5}}.
distance-from-zero.why: Reza wrote {{alg:|-7| = -7}}. Why is this wrong?
distance-from-zero.model: {{alg:|-7|}} is the distance from {{num:-7}} to zero. A distance is never negative: it is 7 steps. So {{alg:|-7| = 7}}. Likewise {{alg:-(-5)}} is the opposite of {{num:-5}}, which is 5, not {{num:-5}}.

feedback.count: There are two floors that are 5 away from 0. Place both.
feedback.one-side: Both of your points are on the same floor. Look on the other side of zero too.
feedback.wrong: Count 5 steps from 0 to the right, and 5 steps from 0 to the left.

order-matters.title: Does the order matter?
order-matters.prompt: The dots show {{alg:8 - 5 = 3}} and {{alg:5 - 8 = -3}}: swapping the numbers changed the answer. Which of these gives the same answer when you swap the two numbers?
order-matters.hint: Work each one out both ways. For example, {{alg:12 ÷ (-3)}} and {{alg:(-3) ÷ 12}}.
order-matters.success: Correct! {{alg:(-4) × 3 = -12}} and {{alg:3 × (-4) = -12}}. Multiplication (and addition) are {{term:commutative-property}}: order does not matter.
order-matters.why: Why can you swap the numbers in a multiplication but not in a subtraction?
order-matters.model: {{alg:(-4) × 3}} and {{alg:3 × (-4)}} are both three lots of {{num:-4}}, so they are equal. But {{alg:8 - 5}} starts at 8 and hops left 5, landing on 3, while {{alg:5 - 8}} starts at 5 and hops left 8, landing on {{num:-3}}. Subtraction and division do not have the commutative property.

feedback.subtraction-swapped: Look at the dots: {{alg:8 - 5 = 3}} but {{alg:5 - 8 = -3}}. Subtraction gives the opposite answer when you swap.
feedback.division-swapped: {{alg:12 ÷ (-3) = -4}}, but {{alg:(-3) ÷ 12}} is only a quarter of {{num:-1}}. Division changes when you swap.
feedback.wrong: Try each one both ways round.
